Journal · Biokovo

Biokovo by e-bike: what to expect

26 June 2026

Biokovo is not a gentle mountain. It rises almost directly from the Makarska riviera — the sea on one side, limestone karst on the other — and the ascent demands commitment even on an e-bike. What electric assist changes is the ratio of effort to reward. This is what the ride actually involves.

What is Biokovo, and where is it?

Biokovo is a limestone massif in central Dalmatia, running roughly 36 kilometres along the coast between Split and the Neretva delta. Its highest point, Sveti Jure, reaches 1,762 metres — the second highest peak in Croatia. The mountain forms the natural border between coastal Dalmatia and the Dalmatian hinterland, with the Cetina canyon running along its eastern flank.

The Makarska riviera — the strip of coast below Biokovo between Brela and Gradac — is defined by the mountain as much as by the sea. The proximity is what makes the ascent by e-MTB interesting: you leave the coast, climb through scrub oak and limestone, and in two to three hours the Adriatic is 1,500 metres below you.

What does the e-MTB ascent of Biokovo involve?

The main route ascends from the coast near Makarska via a combination of the Biokovo road and off-road trail sections, gaining approximately 1,500 metres over 20–25 kilometres. The road is paved but steep — gradients of 8–12% are sustained for extended sections. The trail variants are rougher and shorter in distance but technically more demanding.

The ride takes four to six hours depending on route choice, pace, and how long you stop at the skywalk platform and the ridge viewpoints. Vehicle support travels the route alongside you; the e-bike is always optional.

At the top: a lunar landscape of white limestone, the occasional chamois (divokoza), and in clear conditions a view that covers the full Dalmatian island chain — Brač, Hvar, Vis, Korčula — and reaches to the Italian coast on very clear days.

What is the Biokovo skywalk, and is it worth it?

The Biokovo skywalk (Skywalk Biokovo) is a glass-floored viewing platform that extends from the cliff face at approximately 1,228 metres elevation, with the sea directly below. It opened in 2019 and sits within Biokovo Nature Park.

Standing on it gives a clean 180-degree view of the Adriatic — the platform cantilevers over the cliff far enough that the ground beneath your feet is open sea. The glass floor is not for everyone; the railings are solid and the experience is controlled, but the sense of exposure is genuine.

Access requires entering the nature park (entry fee applies). The platform is reachable by the road vehicle for those not cycling, which means it is worth including regardless of whether you complete the full ascent.

How hard is the Biokovo climb on an e-bike? What does electric assist actually change?

The honest answer: the e-MTB makes the climb possible for people who would not otherwise attempt it. Without assist, the Biokovo road requires a strong cyclist with specific training. With assist (typically 250W Bosch or Shimano systems on high-end bikes), the sustained gradients become manageable for riders of moderate general fitness.

What electric assist does not change: it is still a long day. The battery depletes faster at high gradients and in hot conditions. High-end e-MTBs carry 625–750Wh batteries; a full Biokovo ascent in summer heat will use 70–90% of capacity. Vehicle support carries a spare battery on Adrion journeys.

Expect to arrive at the top with effort in your legs. The electric assist flattens the suffering curve — it does not eliminate the ride.

What is the best season to cycle Biokovo by e-bike?

May, June, September, and early October. The mountain road within Biokovo Nature Park typically opens in late April and closes after the first significant snowfall, usually November.

May and June: the mountain is green and in flower. Temperatures at the summit are 8–12°C cooler than the coast. Winds can be strong — the Bura (bura) blows through gaps in the ridge and can reach 60–80 km/h in gusts. Check the forecast; the ride is unpleasant and exposed in high bura conditions.

July–August: the summit is clear and the views are at their best, but the lower section of the ascent from the coast is hot. An early start (7:00–7:30am) is essential.

September: the most reliable month. The bura is less frequent, temperatures are pleasant from coast to summit, and the light at elevation in autumn is exceptional. The best overall option.

What is the vehicle support, and can you opt out of the ride?

On an Adrion Biokovo journey, a Mercedes V-Class with driver follows the route throughout. The support vehicle carries equipment, spare batteries, water, food, and anything else the group needs. It is a proper support vehicle, not a token presence.

Opting out is straightforward at any point. The road is driveable to the skywalk platform; passengers who prefer not to ride can be at the summit before the cyclists and in the same vehicle for the descent. The e-MTB is the recommended way to experience the ascent, but it is an option within the programme, not a condition of participation.

Frequently asked

+ How hard is the Biokovo climb on an e-bike?

Demanding but accessible for riders of moderate general fitness. The ascent gains approximately 1,500 metres over 20–25 kilometres, with sustained gradients of 8–12%. Electric assist makes the climb possible for people who would not attempt it on a standard bike, but expect a full day of effort. Vehicle support is present throughout.

+ Is the Biokovo skywalk worth visiting?

Yes. The glass-floored platform at 1,228 metres cantilevering over the cliff face gives a clear, unobstructed view of the Dalmatian island chain — Brač, Hvar, Vis, and further. It is reachable by vehicle for those not cycling, so it can be included regardless of how much of the ascent you complete.

+ Can beginners do the Biokovo e-bike ascent?

People with no prior mountain biking experience can do the road route — the surface is paved and the technique is straightforward. The challenge is the length and gradient rather than technical difficulty. Riders who are generally fit and comfortable on a bicycle can manage it with electric assist. Trail variants require more experience.

+ When is the best season to cycle Biokovo?

September is the most reliable month: the bura wind is less frequent, the mountain light is exceptional, and temperatures are comfortable from coast to summit. May and June are also excellent. July and August work with an early start but the lower ascent is hot. The park road is typically open late April through November.

+ Do I need to be in the nature park to cycle Biokovo?

The main ascent route passes through Biokovo Nature Park (Park prirode Biokovo). An entry fee applies. The park road is maintained and signposted. The skywalk platform requires a separate entry ticket. Adrion includes park entry and logistics as part of the journey.
